title: fix(plugin-detail): a related list resolves `user` columns to names, like every other list
body:
Fixes #10112

`Clause-②: no` — declared on the claim, unchanged on delivery, and checked
mechanically rather than asserted: the diff adds no exported symbol, no member
to `RelatedListProps` and no published prop (`git diff BASE HEAD -- RelatedList.tsx`
contains no `export` / interface-member line). `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test`
over this branch's three paths prints `NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) checked against
5 governed surface(s); none matched`. This pulls one renderer back onto an
already-declared contract; no accepted set widens.

Seat session, in prose because footers do not survive an edit:
`session_01Xr7APep6jm1Zta3KUzPzZf`.

## Premise, re-taken on `origin/main` `7725c10a0`

The card's framing holds at source, both halves:

- `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` in `packages/core/src/utils/expand-fields.ts` is
  `lookup` / `master_detail` / `tree` / `user`. `user` is in the canonical
  reference-bearing family today, so the card's contract section is current and
  this is a renderer outlier, not invalid metadata.
- `RelatedList.tsx`'s auto-fetch built its `find` params with `$filter`,
  `$top`, `$skip` and `$orderby` and no `$expand` at all; its batch
  label-hydration loop opened with a private
  `def.type !== 'lookup' && def.type !== 'master_detail'` skip; and its cell
  metadata injected resolved labels under the same two-member test. All three
  sites the card names were present.

The ordinary list's resolver path, which the dispatch left open as step 1, is
`buildExpandFields` from `@object-ui/core` — `ListView` calls it, and so do
kanban, grid, gallery, calendar, gantt, map, timeline, tree, the dashboard
table and `DetailView`. It lives in `@object-ui/core`, so reaching it needed
nothing from `packages/fields/`: no stop-and-report, and no second user-name
resolver.

## The repair — two halves, one family

**The auto-fetch now sends `$expand`.** The roots come from `buildExpandFields`
over the child object's schema, which is the same projection every other list
in the tree sends. Three decisions worth naming, each with its reason in the
code:

- The column restriction is resolved through *this* component's identity
  spelling — `accessorKey` first, then `columnIdentity`. `buildExpandFields`
  decides "the caller restricted the columns" from the raw array's LENGTH and
  then keeps only what `columnIdentity` resolves, and `accessorKey` is not one
  of its keys. Handing it the authored array raw would have restricted the
  expansion to the empty set and expanded nothing, silently — on a column shape
  this component supports everywhere else and already has tests for.
- The parent relationship is never expanded: `filterFK` removes it from every
  column list this component draws, so a sub-read for it could only be waste.
- FLS gates the OUTPUT, the shape objectui#7215 / objectui#7230 ruled and
  `DetailView` already uses. `$expand` asks the server to resolve a reference
  and hand back the related record — strictly more than the bare key this fetch
  already receives. Gating the input would WIDEN, because an emptied column
  list reads as "no restriction". This is why `usePermissions()` moved to the
  top of the component: same call, unconditional, now nameable by the fetch
  effect.

The dependency that carries it onto the wire is a CONTENT key, not the array.
The child object's schema arrives asynchronously and the fetch effect is
deliberately not gated on it, so the first query goes out before the schema
exists and is byte-identical to the one this component has always sent; when
the schema lands and yields roots, the key changes and the effect re-runs once,
now asking for them. A child object with no expandable column keeps an empty
key, `''` to `''`, and re-runs exactly as often as before — the same
direction-of-the-default argument the arity flag above it already makes.

**The batch fallback now asks the family.** It served rows a caller supplied,
and a backend that does not honour `$expand`, through a predicate naming two of
the family's four members — so a primitive `user` id was never gathered there
either. It now calls `isExpandableFieldType`. A `user` cell reads no
`field.options`, so the `options` injection stays on the two types that do read
it and the resolved name reaches the user cell as the record shape that cell
documents. The name still comes from the one batch map in this file, resolved
through the target object's declared `nameField` / `titleFormat` — no second
resolver exists.

## The pins, and the two defects the ablations found in them

`RelatedList.userColumnNames-10112.test.tsx`. Six rows: the auto-fetch case,
the wire case, the caller-data case, a control, and one withdrawal probe per
site. The assertion is the rendered NAME and the absence of the stored id, with
the card's own 32-character value as the fixture.

⚠️ Two of those rows were WRONG when first written, and running the ablations
is what said so — recorded here rather than quietly corrected.

1. **The identity pins were vacuous.** They recorded calls to the `has` of the
   object core exports, the shape objectui#5874 uses in this package. That
   instrument does not transfer here: TWO sites consult the family on the same
   render, so a call recorded by either satisfies a recorder installed for the
   other, and a private copy at one site is masked by its neighbour. They now
   WITHDRAW `user` from the exported set and read that one site's own output,
   each with the ordinary lookup as a positive control so the negative half is a
   reading rather than an absence.
2. **The control was entangled with the mechanism it controls.** It waited on
   the `sys_user` fetch — which the batch-half ablation removes — so it went red
   under that ablation, reporting the mechanism twice instead of controlling it.
   It waits on the lookup target now.

**Ablation, four legs, each restored and proven byte-equal to HEAD afterwards**
(`git checkout HEAD -- path`, blob hash compared, `git diff HEAD` empty; run
through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which takes the on-disk proof itself). Directions
were written down before running:

| leg | mutation | measured |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A | drop the `$expand` line | 3 red — both auto-fetch cases and the auto-fetch probe; caller-data, control and batch probe green |
| B | restore the private two-member disjunction in the batch loop | 1 red — the caller-data case |
| C | give the batch loop a MEMBER-IDENTICAL private set | 1 red — the batch probe ONLY; its behavioural case stays green |
| D | give the `$expand` site a MEMBER-IDENTICAL private set | 1 red — that site's probe ONLY; the behavioural and wire cases stay green |

C and D are the point of the probes: they produce the one failure a behavioural
case structurally cannot, and they produce it at the site that holds the copy.

## Gates

Run at `fa33919af`, exit codes captured to files and read from the files.

| command | exit |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` (repo root) | 0 — 194 files, 1966 tests passed |
| `tsc --noEmit` (plugin-detail) | 0 |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` (plugin-detail) | 0 |

| `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `-inherit` / `-override-shape` | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 — 1 source file of 1 released package, 1 changeset |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | 0 |

The dependency closure (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' build`)
was built before any typecheck was believed — the first `tsc` run reported
fifteen `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/*'` errors purely from an
unbuilt workspace, which is a stale-`dist` reading and not a verdict. Vitest
resolves `@object-ui/*` to `src` through the root config's alias map, so the
test runs are on sources.

⚠️ NOT MEASURED locally, left to CI: the nine merge-queue required checks
(`Lint`, `Type Check`, the four `Test` shards, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`,
`Changeset Declaration`). `pnpm lint` is a repo-wide scan CI owns; the
package-scoped runs above are what this branch owes.

## Acceptance notes

- **The wire now carries two queries on first mount for a child object with an
  expandable column**, and that is a deliberate, documented trade rather than an
  oversight. Gating the row fetch on the schema fetch was the alternative and is
  refused in this file already, on the ground that a `DataSource` without
  `getObjectSchema` would then never fetch rows at all — trading one extra round
  trip for a silently empty list on every related list in the app. The
  multi-value arity flag beside it already accepts the same refetch for the same
  reason.
- **Multi-valued `user` columns are unchanged and still unresolved on the
  fallback path.** The batch loop gathers string and number values only, never
  array members — true for `lookup` before this branch and true for `user`
  after it. `$expand` resolves them server-side, so the auto-fetch path is
  fixed either way; the fallback's array blind spot is pre-existing, identical
  across the family, and out of this card's scope. Noted, not filed: nothing in
  the tree consumes it today and no PR is heading for that loop.
- **`packages/fields/` was not touched** (objectui#10172 holds it) and needed
  no change: `UserCellRenderer` already draws a name and avatar from an expanded
  record, and already draws a marked unresolved-reference affordance from a
  primitive. The repair is entirely about which value reaches it.
